title: Re-commission PROP-graph archaeology (originally DIRECTIVE-20260628-004, false-closed via PROP-120 mislinkage) + audit the 20 pending operator-directives — walk both graphs and classify.

context.why_now: DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 was auto-closed 2026-07-02 by PROP-108 because PROP-120 (auto-close-gap fix for propose-only directives) declared directive_id=DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 and PROP-120 reached integrated. But PROP-120 does not fulfill the archaeology intent — the walk of ~127 PROPs and the trust-graph cleanup were never done. This mislink-close is itself an instance of the miscount class the archaeology directive was supposed to surface. Meanwhile git shows 20 pending operator-directives, 12 aged >=20 days, most with no auto-close reach (no linked PROP or opt-in). Operator wants both problems attacked in one deliverable so they audit each other.

prior_directive_reference.reason_for_false_close: PROP-120 declared directive_id=DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 as its authoring source (which is defensible — PROP-120's problem was discovered while thinking about the archaeology audit's trust-graph). PROP-108's Mechanism A closed the directive because linked PROP.status=integrated matched the terminal whitelist. But PROP-120 addresses a completely different problem than the archaeology walk. The commissioned deliverable was never produced.
prior_directive_reference.operator_decision: Do NOT reopen DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 in place. Preserve its historical record. This new directive supersedes it.

context.operator_priors_on_zombie_shape: Best guess for the 20 pending directives: ~40% obviously superseded by shipped PROPs (mechanical close, no follow-up); ~30% still owed (real infra debt: PROP-113/114 root-cause, PROP-104 Phase 0 report, workspace-sync + integrity cost audits); ~20% aged out (concerns resolved by adjacent work, no PROP needed); ~10% unclear. Operator wants tinker's judgment on classification, not a rubber-stamp.

part_A_pending_directive_audit.scope: All operator-directives in monitor/tinker/operator-directives/ with status='pending' as of tinker's run start.
part_A_pending_directive_audit.method: For each pending directive, classify into one of four buckets: (A) trivially superseded — a shipped PROP clearly addresses the same problem, close with directive_id back-ref if missing; (B) genuinely still owed — real infra debt, needs a linked PROP or a spawned sub-directive; (C) aged out — concern was overtaken by events, close with reasoning; (D) unclear — surface to operator with a specific yes/no question.
part_A_pending_directive_audit.output: Table in the deliverable: directive_id | age_days | class | evidence | recommended_action. Then execute: bucket A gets mechanical close (backfill directive_id field on the closer PROP where possible, then let PROP-108 auto-close on next run OR manually close if no linked PROP exists); bucket C gets manual close with closure_note; buckets B + D surface to operator.

part_B_prop_graph_archaeology.scope: All monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-*.json as of tinker's run start (approximate: ~127 PROPs).
part_B_prop_graph_archaeology.method: Build a dependency graph via three edge types: (1) supersedes_props / superseded_by_props declarations; (2) same directive_id linkage (multiple PROPs from same commission); (3) textual references (PROP-X in the summary/context of PROP-Y). For each PROP, verify status is consistent with reality: status='implemented' should have an actually-shipped-and-verified-passing verification_pattern; status='integrated' should be visible in the closer PROPs or shipped code; status='proposed' with age>60d should be checked for OBE.
part_B_prop_graph_archaeology.categories_to_surface: (a) OBE-but-not-marked — proposed/pending PROPs whose problem was solved by adjacent work; (b) wrongly-marked-implemented — status claims terminal but the shipped artifact doesn't match; (c) broken-chain — supersedes_props points at PROP-X but PROP-X still status=proposed instead of superseded; (d) mislink false-close risk — PROPs whose directive_id was set opportunistically and would false-close a different-intent commission (PROP-120 → DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 is the seed example).

part_C_trust_graph_report.scope: Combined finding from Part A + Part B: what does PROP-102 Mechanism A (verification_pattern FIXED) trust look like across the graph, and what does PROP-108 Mechanism A + Mechanism B (via directive_id back-ref) trust look like across the graph. Are there enough mislinks or wrongly-marked-implemented PROPs to justify keeping PROP-102 in shadow mode? Should PROP-108's enforce mode be reverted pending cleanup?
part_C_trust_graph_report.deliverable: One clear recommendation: keep PROP-108 enforce ON / OFF / add per-directive vetting step. Same for PROP-102 shadow → enforce flip readiness.

deliverable_acceptance_criteria: One PROP or a small suite of PROPs authored covering Parts A, B, C. Each PROP has a verification_pattern (grade B or higher).
Part A: at least the trivially-superseded set is closed (or has an operator-approval question pending in a HNOTE to steve).
Part B: at minimum, the OBE-but-not-marked and wrongly-marked-implemented categories are populated with specific PROP-IDs and evidence.
Part C: a clear ON/OFF/vet recommendation on PROP-108 enforce mode and PROP-102 enforce-flip readiness.

The archaeology walk itself is documented — even a summary-level report file at monitor/tinker/reports/prop-graph-archaeology-20260704.md is acceptable, so long as the categorization is machine-checkable.

constraints.if_too_large_for_one_run: Split into Part A (author + ship first) → Part B (walk + report) → Part C (final recommendation). Track cross-run state via monitor/tinker/reports/prop-graph-archaeology-progress.json.
constraints.do_not_bulk_close_without_evidence: Every close must cite the superseding PROP (bucket A) or the aged-out reason (bucket C). No 'close because it's old'.
constraints.do_not_flip_enforce_mode_without_operato: Part C's recommendation is advisory only. Operator flips flag files.

prior_directives_that_are_relevant: DIRECTIVE-20260619-001-auto-close-zombie-directives-mechanism-b-extension.json (concept precedent — extend Mechanism B via supersedes graph)
DIRECTIVE-20260701-001-zombie-directive-audit-and-backfill.json (previous 3-day pending-directive backfill; sets template for close-with-directive_id backfill pattern)

not_in_scope: Reopening DIRECTIVE-20260628-004 in place (operator explicitly declined this).
Changing PROP-108 or PROP-102 enforcement in this run (advisory only).
Auditing analyst, decider, or other agents' output — the graph is PROPs + operator-directives only.
operator_notes: This directive intentionally does NOT set auto_close_when_deliverable_proposed=true. The deliverable is real work (walk + classify + recommend) and I want to see the artifact before it closes. Auto-close via PROP-108 Mechanism A on a linked PROP reaching integrated is fine.
